title: PuDHammer: Experimental Analysis of Read Disturbance Effects of Processing-using-DRAM in Real DRAM Chips
problem: Processing-using-DRAM (PuD) operations require multiple-row activation (activating multiple DRAM rows simultaneously or in quick succession), a fundamentally different access pattern from conventional single-row activation. No prior work has characterized whether this multiple-row activation exacerbates DRAM read disturbance (RowHammer-style bitflips) compared to standard single-row activation.
motivation: PuD is increasingly proposed as a near-memory compute paradigm to overcome the memory bandwidth wall, but deploying it safely requires understanding its interaction with DRAM read disturbance — a worsening reliability and security vulnerability — before it can be used in real systems.
method: The authors conduct an experimental characterization study (PuDHammer) using 316 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major manufacturers. They test multiple-row activation patterns (as used by PuD bulk bitwise operations) across a sweep of operational parameters: temperature, data patterns, access patterns (simultaneous vs. sequential row activation), DRAM timing parameters, and spatial variation within chips. They measure the minimum hammer count (HC_first) required to induce the first bitflip and compare to conventional single-row RowHammer.
key_novelty: First experimental characterization of how PuD-style multiple-row activation affects DRAM read disturbance on real DDR4 chips, showing PuDHammer can reduce the bitflip threshold by up to 158.58x compared to standard RowHammer.
contributions: First characterization of PuDHammer read disturbance on 316 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four manufacturers, covering diverse operational conditions.
Quantification that PuDHammer reduces the minimum hammer count for first bitflip (HC_first) by up to 158.58x compared to conventional RowHammer.
Analysis showing PuDHammer is affected by temperature, data patterns, timing parameters, and spatial variation within a chip.
Demonstration that combining RowHammer with PuDHammer is more effective than either attack alone, raising security and reliability implications for PuD deployments.

metrics.other: HC_first (minimum hammer count to first bitflip) reduced by up to 158.58x vs. RowHammer on 316 real DDR4 chips

baselines: conventional single-row RowHammer on DDR4 DRAM
limitations: Study is limited to DDR4 chips from four manufacturers and does not directly evaluate mitigation strategies for PuDHammer in existing or proposed PuD systems.
primary_theme: DRAM read disturbance characterization for PuD operations
